---
id: "smk-11"
title: "Haskell"
---

Haskell is a purely functional programming language named after the logician Haskell Curry. It was designed by a committee in the late 1980s to consolidate research on lazy functional languages, and the first version of the language report was published in 1990. Haskell uses lazy evaluation by default, so expressions are evaluated only when their values are needed, and it has a strong static type system with type inference, type classes and parametric polymorphism. Side effects such as input and output are handled through monads, which keep pure and impure code separate. The most widely used implementation is the Glasgow Haskell Compiler, which compiles to native code and supports many extensions to the standard language. Haskell has influenced the design of other languages, including Scala, Rust and Swift, and it is used in academia, in financial software and in tools such as the Pandoc document converter.
